summary: This is a clipped pandas 2.2.2 API reference page for Series.dt.tz_localize, which localizes tz-naive datetime Series/Index objects to tz-aware ones (or removes timezone info by passing tz=None) without moving the time to another zone. The page documents the tz, ambiguous and nonexistent parameters, the return and error behavior, and gives examples for US/Eastern localization, removing timezones, inferring DST transitions, and shifting nonexistent times in Europe/Warsaw. Navigation menus and repeated boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: pandas 2.2.2 API reference page describing Series.dt.tz_localize, which makes tz-naive datetimes timezone-aware and handles DST ambiguities.
key_facts: Series.dt.tz_localize localizes tz-naive Datetime Array/Index to tz-aware Datetime Array/Index without moving the time to another time zone.
Passing tz=None to tz_localize removes time zone information while preserving local time.
The tz parameter accepts str, pytz.timezone, dateutil.tz.tzfile, datetime.tzinfo or None.
The ambiguous parameter defaults to 'raise' and accepts 'infer', 'NaT', or a bool array.
The nonexistent parameter defaults to 'raise' and accepts 'shift_forward', 'shift_backward', 'NaT', or a timedelta.
In Central European Time, 02:30:00 local time occurs both at 00:30:00 UTC and at 01:30:00 UTC during the DST fall-back transition.
Raises TypeError if the Datetime Array/Index is tz-aware and tz is not None.
The documented example localizes pd.date_range('2018-03-01 09:00', periods=3) to the US/Eastern time zone, giving offsets of -05:00.
With nonexistent='shift_forward', the time 2015-03-29 02:30:00 in Europe/Warsaw becomes 03:00:00+02:00.
With nonexistent=pd.Timedelta('1h'), the time 2015-03-29 02:30:00 in Europe/Warsaw becomes 03:30:00+02:00.
The page's see-also reference is DatetimeIndex.tz_convert, which converts tz-aware DatetimeIndex from one time zone to another.
